newsitem.title: FRANCE: Blair repeats Britain needs referendum on Europe.
newsitem.headline: Blair repeats Britain needs referendum on Europe.

text.p: British opposition leader Tony Blair said on Friday there must be a referendum to decide whether Britain should join a single European Union currency unless it was the main issue in an election.
Speaking to reporters after meeting French President Jacques Chirac, the Labour Party leader also said Britain should keep its options open on the possibility of joining a single currency.
The test would be whether it was in Britain's national economic interest to join, Blair said.
"Unless it is the issue at a general election then there must be a referendum," he said. "It has to be done with the consent of the British people."
He added: "What is important to recognise is that the options should be kept open, but the test is Britain's national economic interest."
Asked what problems he envisaged with a single currency, Blair said labour mobility would not be as easy as in a bloc where all people spoke the same language.
Because the likelihood of large fiscal transfers to compensate poor countries would be reduced, there would have to be sustainable economic convergence, he said.
"You have got to make sure for a single currency to work, there has to be economic convergence that is sustainable," he said.
